subject.title: Npm-valid package scopes with dots/underscores cannot map to ClawHub publishers

question: Should ClawHub preserve slug-only publisher handles and introduce verified npm-scope aliases, or instead make npm-compatible scope characters canonical publisher-handle characters?
rationale: Either option changes a durable package-ownership and identity contract across publisher creation, scope matching, transfers, URLs, and authorization; source inspection cannot safely choose that policy boundary.

options.title: Retain slug handles with verified aliases
options.body: Keep public publisher handles URL-safe and add an explicit, unique npm-scope alias with lifecycle checks for publish, transfer, and ownership validation.

options.title: Broaden canonical handle syntax
options.body: Allow npm-compatible dot and underscore characters directly in publisher handles and define their URL, normalization, and collision semantics.

options.title: Require npm package renames
options.body: Keep the existing handle contract and require affected publishers to migrate to matching slug-safe npm scopes.

recommendation.title: Retain slug handles with verified aliases
recommendation.body: Keep public publisher handles URL-safe and add an explicit, unique npm-scope alias with lifecycle checks for publish, transfer, and ownership validation.

likelyOwner.reason: The collaborator supplied the concrete affected-package evidence and is the best available routing contact while repository history ownership remains inconclusive.
